name: cfgkit
tagline: Typed configuration from layered sources, for Go.
description: Typed Go configuration from layered sources — env vars, .env, JSON, YAML, TOML, flags, Vault, Consul, etcd, Kubernetes, AWS, GCP and Azure — into one validated struct. Defaults compile into the binary, so a valid config exists with zero input. Reports which source set each field, masks secrets, and validates in CI instead of at boot.

positioning.audience: Go teams running services across several environments, who need to know why a value is what it is
positioning.wedge: Provenance. Every field can say which source set it, so 'why is my port 9001 when I set 2310' stops being a guessing game — and defaults live in Go, so zero input is a valid configuration rather than a startup failure.
differentiators: Provenance: Result.Explain names the source of every field
Zero input works: compiled-in defaults mean no config file is required to start
Validate without booting: cfgkit.Check fails a CI step instead of a production container
Secrets masked structurally, in Explain and JSON alike, not by output styling
Contract generation: the .env.example is produced from the struct, so it cannot drift
A flag default never wins — only flags the user actually typed count
One dependency in the core; every adapter is a separate module you opt into
The three verbs ship as a mountable cobra command, so an application CLI gets config check/explain/document without writing a main
